table_events.server_send: { type: 'change', table: 'notes', action: 'insert' | 'update' | 'delete' }  (owner-scoped tables send non-owners { type: 'change', action: 'refresh' })
table_events.use_for: Live invalidation when auto-CRUD mutations or flow SQL writes happen. Same {table, action} as SSE 'change' events but bidirectional; never the row.
table_events.subscription: `subscribe` narrows, it does not authorize. A connection that never sends `subscribe` (one opened only to join rooms, as bm.room() does) receives change events for EVERY table it may read, under the same audience rules as SSE. After a subscribe that names tables, named change events arrive only for the subscribed tables: the known names among those sent, added to any earlier subscription. A name the app has no table for is not subscribed and is answered with `{ type: 'error', tables: [<unknown names>], body }` (at most 10 names, each cut to 64 bytes); a subscribe whose names are all unknown leaves the connection with no named events, it does not fall back to every table. Names are the schema's table names, matched exactly, plus `_benmore_notifications` (the caller's own notification events) and `_benmore_presence`; a connection that subscribed gets those two only when it names them. A subscribe with no `tables` (a missing key, an empty list, `room:` in its place) changes nothing and is not answered. Unsubscribing from every subscribed table restores the every-table default. The generic `{ type: 'change', action: 'refresh' }` names no table and always arrives. A room-only client can ignore `type: 'change'` frames.

room_broadcast.client_send:
{ type: 'join' | 'leave', room: 'chat-lobby' }  ←  join first
              { type: 'broadcast', room: 'chat-lobby', payload: <any json> }
room_broadcast.use_for: Chat, presence indicators, WebRTC signaling (SDP/ICE), typing indicators, collaborative cursors.
room_broadcast.note: Clients SEND type 'broadcast' but RECEIVE type 'message' (bm.room() handles this for you). The sender does not get its own relay back.

server_send_from_flow.step: `run: broadcast` with `with: { room, payload }` - see api({at:'flows'}) → broadcast_step for the copy-paste YAML.
server_send_from_flow.frame: { type: 'message', room, from: 'server', payload } - the same frame a client relay produces, so `bm.room(name).on(kind, (payload, from) => …)` receives it unchanged (kind = payload.kind). `from` is the STRING 'server'; client relays carry the sender's numeric user id (or no `from` for an anonymous sender), so `from === 'server'` never matches a user.
server_send_from_flow.reaches: Every connection of THIS app that has joined the room right now and still passes the room's ws_rooms membership rule. In an app with `groups:` only the flow caller's tenant; a run with no signed-in session (cron, async job, public flow) fails there instead of reaching every tenant. Nothing is queued for clients that join later - store anything durable in a table.
server_send_from_flow.limits: Room: 1-128 characters of a-z A-Z 0-9 _ - . : after interpolation. Payload: at most 64 KiB of JSON; larger fails the step. Rooms are per process: in a multi-instance cluster (BENMORE_CLUSTER=true) a room message reaches only members connected to the instance that ran the flow, same as client relays.
